summary: Upgrade BunkPro with (1) a new "Mark Past Attendance" flow that lets users mark attendance for any past date via a calendar, prevents future/duplicate marking, stores per-date attendance records, and safely recalculates streak/points; (2) disable any automatic "auto-absent" handling for missed days; (3) add a once-per-day reminder push notification if today’s attendance is not marked by a configured time, respecting notification settings and deep-linking into the attendance screen on both app and web; and (4) remove the web app splash/initial loading screen entirely so the app loads directly into Login/Dashboard with no intermediate splash UI or cached splash artifacts.
architectural_notes: Android app using MVVM architecture (preferred) with clean structure and error handling
Offline-first app using local Room/SQLite database (secure local storage)
Do not alter BunkWell-equivalent attendance calculation logic; focus changes on UI/UX, performance, and visual polish
Compatibility with latest Android SDK; prioritize stability (zero crashes, no memory leaks)
Ensure the user-provided BunkPro logo is integrated into the app branding (app icon/header as applicable) and splash/launch screen during final polish.
Ensure no third-party/white-label branding (e.g., “Build with Caffeine AI”) appears anywhere in the app UI, splash screen, settings/about, or build artifacts.
Notifications scope added: implement web push notifications, desktop notifications, and local notifications (clarify platform support/approach for Android vs web/desktop).
Branding scope: create new BunkPro logo assets (icon-only + full wordmark) with dark/light variants; must be flat, minimal, and legible at small sizes (48x48).
New scope: introduce user identity/profile (name) persistence and a points/streak system, plus weekly ranking logic organized under a dedicated “rank” module/folder.

Weekly ranking must be computed deterministically with a stored weekly snapshot and last-run timestamp (Sunday 12:00 AM), using stable sort criteria (points, streak, join date) and preventing duplicate recalculation; support offline mode.
known_issues: "Send test notification" does not show/appear (notification seems inactive/not visible) when pressed.
Build/deployment failed with error: "Unable to create your app" when attempting the placeholder text update build.
Build attempt failed with error message: “AI was unable to complete your request. Try rephrasing it more clearly.” (deployment did not complete).
UI regression: “Mark Today’s Classes” and “View Rankings” buttons changed to black; should be purple per app theme.
Global Ranking visibility bug: users are not mutually visible (leaderboard appears device-specific/partially loaded/incorrectly filtered; may only show current user or be truncated).
Critical: After logout, the app shows an “Unauthorized User” error (logout flow is not clearing auth/session state and/or API calls continue after logout).
Push notifications not working after APK installation (no notifications received).
Calendar header UI issue: month name and navigation arrows are overlapping/too close; needs centered month text with left/right arrows at extremes and proper padding.

Bug: In 'Mark Past Attendance' flow, calendar date selection updates visually but subjects do not display after selecting a date (selectedDate not persisted / subject filtering by weekday not triggered; UI not re-rendering).

Splash screen still shows purple/pink background and old logo on initial load (branding not updated; possible index.html/body/theme_color/service-worker cache causing a purple flash and stale assets).

existing_features.title: Implement the core data model and logic for subject-wise attendance tracking, including: subjects (add/edit/delete), per-subject counters for Attended/Missed/Cancelled/Extra classes, class exchanges, per-subject attendance percentage, overall attendance percentage, reset attendance for a subject, and a target attendance percentage setting used by calculators. All calculations must correctly handle edge cases such as 0 total classes and 100% attendance.

Create an offline-first local persistence layer for all app data (subjects, timetable, class history/events, settings like target % and theme). Data must be stored locally in the browser (e.g., IndexedDB) and loaded on startup, with robust error handling and no data loss on refresh.

Implement local backup & restore (minimum local backup): allow exporting all app data to a file and importing it back, including validation, versioning, and a clear warning that restore replaces current data.

Build the Home Dashboard screen with: overall attendance %, subject-wise cards, animated circular progress indicators per subject, quick “Mark Today” action, and insight callouts such as “You can bunk X more classes” and “Attend next Y classes to reach Z%” based on the current target percentage.
Implement subject management UI flows: add subject, edit subject, delete subject with a confirmation dialog, and reset subject attendance with a confirmation dialog.

Create the Timetable screen with a clean weekly grid layout for day-wise subjects, including: tapping to edit subjects in a slot, long-press (or equivalent) to add an extra class, and support for recording class exchanges tied to the timetable.
Create the Subject Details screen for a selected subject including: attendance stats summary, calendar view of class events, an attendance trend graph, safe bunk calculator, and a reset button.

Create the Settings screen including: Dark/Light mode toggle, target attendance % setting, app theme selector, Backup & Restore actions, and an About section that displays “BunkPro” and tagline “Track Smart. Bunk Smarter.”

Add navigation structure with a smooth bottom navigation bar connecting: Home, Timetable, and Settings, plus deep navigation to Subject Details from subject cards. Ensure smooth micro-animations and transitions without jank.

Implement the premium UI/UX redesign for BunkPro with a consistent modern aesthetic: soft gradients (purple-blue and midnight-dark themes), glassmorphism or soft neumorphism styling, rounded cards (16–20px radius), elegant modern sans-serif typography, minimal clutter, and subtle motion design (e.g., progress indicator animations, button press feedback). Do not change any core attendance logic while applying these design improvements.

Implement optional premium features (non-blocking, can be toggled/disabled if needed): simple predictive insights (based on recent attendance trend), motivational streak counter, and a “Danger Zone” alert state when attendance drops below the target threshold.

Add generated branding assets and wire them into the UI: a premium minimal logo for “BunkPro” with an academic vibe (calendar + graph combined concept) and an elegant splash/hero graphic used on initial load screen (web equivalent).

Provide robust error handling and performance safeguards: prevent crashes on invalid inputs, handle storage failures, keep initial load fast, and avoid memory leaks (e.g., clean up timers/animations).

Integrate the user-uploaded logo image (unnamed-1.jpg) as the app’s primary branding asset by converting it into static generated assets and wiring them into all existing logo placements (initial loading splash and Settings → About).
Add a browser favicon using the user-provided logo mark so the tab icon shows BunkPro branding.

Perform a final QA + UI polish pass across Home, Timetable, Subject Details, and Settings to ensure visual consistency, smooth micro-animations (no jank), and correct responsive layout on small screens, without changing core attendance logic.

Replace the current BunkPro branding assets used by the app with the newly uploaded logo image so the logo appears exactly as provided (no redesign), and ensure the updated logo is used everywhere the app currently displays the logo (including the initial loading splash and Settings → About).
Remove/hide all “Built with Caffeine AI” / caffeine.ai attribution and links from the UI so the app does not display Caffeine branding anywhere in-app.

Replace the app’s branding assets so the uploaded file (image.png) is the only logo used, shown exactly as provided (no redesign/re-draw), in all existing logo placements including: Initial loading splash, Settings → About, and any other in-app logo usage.
Update the browser tab icon/favicon to match the uploaded logo (image.png) exactly as provided.
Add notification support using the browser Notifications API, including: permission prompt flow, an in-app toggle to enable/disable notifications, and a test notification action in Settings.

Implement “local notifications” behavior for this web app as on-device/in-app notifications triggered by app events while the app is running (e.g., after successfully saving a class mark), respecting the notifications setting and browser permission state.
Persist the new notification-related user preference(s) in the existing local persistence/backup/restore flow (IndexedDB + export/import backup), without breaking existing stored data.

Add clear user-facing copy in Settings clarifying the supported notification behavior and limitations for this web app (e.g., notifications require browser permission; no guaranteed delivery when the app is closed).

Generate a new modern, minimal, professional BunkPro logo set that follows the provided style requirements (flat, clean, premium/tech, Gen‑Z, recognizable at 48×48) and includes: (1) app icon only (square), (2) full horizontal logo with text, each in both dark-background and light-background variants, using the palette centered on deep purple #6C4DFF (optionally an indigo gradient) with soft white/light gray and an optional subtle neon blue/pink accent; typography must be modern geometric sans-serif with rounded edges, with “Bunk” bold and “Pro” lighter, and the tagline text exactly “Track Smart.”.

Add the newly generated logo assets to the app as static files under frontend/public/assets/generated and wire them into all existing branding placements (at minimum: Initial loading splash and Settings → About), selecting the appropriate dark/light variant based on current theme.

Update the app’s branding constants so that (a) the tagline displayed in the UI uses the exact text “Track Smart.” and (b) the logo path(s) support theme-aware dark/light selection without editing any immutable frontend paths.
Generate and set a matching favicon based on the new app icon, and ensure frontend/index.html references the updated favicon file under frontend/public/assets/generated.

Update the Settings → About section to display the exact text "Founded by Basavaraj Hiremath" (English, with this exact capitalization) in addition to the existing About content, without removing existing app name/tagline/version/copyright.

Debug and fix the Settings → Notifications → "Send Test Notification" action so that pressing the button reliably results in a visible browser notification when notifications are supported, permission is granted, and notifications are enabled; additionally, provide clear in-app feedback when a test notification cannot be sent (e.g., unsupported browser, permission not granted/denied, or send failure).

Add the newly uploaded logo image (ea2777cf-279d-4438-9134-41dc0fd0b5d9.png) to the app as static assets under frontend/public/assets/generated, preserving the logo exactly as provided (no redesign, no re-draw).

Update the app’s branding constants so all existing logo usages (including the initial loading splash and Settings → About) render the newly uploaded logo assets, using the same image for both dark and light themes (theme-aware switching may remain but must resolve to the uploaded logo in both modes).
Update the browser favicon to match the newly uploaded logo exactly by pointing frontend/index.html to the new favicon asset under frontend/public/assets/generated.

Create new high-resolution BunkPro logo artwork matching the user’s spec: circular emblem with a smooth purple-to-blue gradient ring; inside the circle a graduation cap combined with a bold checkmark; include a small rising bar-graph element; clean minimal futuristic look with subtle 3D depth; soft glow under the logo; dark navy background for contrast; typography in a bold modern sans-serif with “Bunk” in a purple gradient and “Pro” in a blue gradient, with slight glow and smooth shadow; ensure it remains legible and recognizable at small sizes and works well in a circular mobile icon crop.

Integrate the newly generated BunkPro logo assets into the app so all existing logo placements use the new artwork: update frontend/src/lib/branding.ts to return the new generated asset paths for both getAppIcon and getHorizontalLogo (use the same images for both dark and light themes unless separate variants are explicitly provided). Ensure the Initial Loading Splash and Settings → About automatically reflect the updated branding without changing their components’ logic.
Update the browser favicon to match the newly generated BunkPro logo by pointing frontend/index.html’s favicon link to the new generated favicon asset under frontend/public/assets/generated.

Add an initial Login screen that is shown on app start when no user name has been set yet, with a single name input and a continue/login action. The login form must validate that the entered value is a “good name” (letters and spaces only, trimmed, non-empty, and within a reasonable length) and display an English validation error when invalid. After a successful login, persist the user name in app state so it remains available throughout the app and across refreshes via the existing IndexedDB persistence.

Extend the frontend domain state and reducer to support a user profile and gamification fields needed for streak points, including at minimum: user name, total points, streak tracking metadata needed to compute a continuous day streak, and a record of which streak milestones have already been awarded so points are not repeatedly re-awarded for the same milestone.

Implement continuous day streak detection based on recorded ClassEvent activity: treat a day as “completed” if at least one ClassEvent exists for that calendar date; compute the current streak as the number of consecutive completed days ending at today (using local time date strings already stored in events). When the streak reaches 3 days for the first time, award +5 points and show an English congratulatory message: “Congrats on your hat-trick! +5 points.” When the streak reaches 6 days for the first time, award +10 points and show an English congratulatory message: “Congrats on your 6-day streak! +10 points.”

Create a separate frontend folder named "rank" to contain all ranking-related UI and logic. Add a Rank screen that can be navigated to from the app (e.g., via a Settings link/button) without breaking existing navigation. The Rank screen must show an English weekly leaderboard list of users ordered by points for the current week, including each user’s rank number, display name, and points.

Wire the frontend streak points awarding to the backend ranking system: when the app awards +5 or +10 points for a milestone, it must also submit the points increment to the backend for the logged-in user and ensure the user’s display name is registered/updated in the backend. The Rank screen must fetch the weekly ranking list from the backend and display it.

Update local persistence and backup/restore to include the new user profile and gamification fields (user name, points, streak metadata, and milestone award state) while remaining backward compatible with existing stored data and older backups by merging missing fields with defaults.
Update the name input example/placeholder text on the Login screen to remove "Chittya" and replace it with "name_clg name" (i.e., the placeholder should read exactly: "e.g., name_clg name").
Update the Login screen name input placeholder example by removing the word "Chittya" and setting the placeholder text to exactly: "e.g., name_clg name".

Add an edit option in Settings → Your Profile to allow the logged-in user to change their saved display name after initial login. The flow must include an explicit UI control (e.g., “Edit” button), an input to update the name, and Save/Cancel actions.

Validate the edited name using the same rules as the Login screen: trimmed, non-empty, 2–50 characters, and only letters (A–Z/a–z) and spaces. Show English validation errors when invalid and prevent saving until valid.

Persist the updated display name through the existing IndexedDB persistence and backup/restore flows, and sync the updated display name to the leaderboard backend by calling the existing display-name registration flow after a successful save (when a backend actor is available). Provide clear English feedback if syncing fails (non-blocking).

Update the Rank screen (frontend/src/rank/RankPage.tsx) leaderboard list UI to display every user in rank order with visually attractive rank-number badges for all ranks (1, 2, 3, … up to N users), not only icons for the top 3.

Upgrade the frontend bottom navigation to include a dedicated Rank tab so the app has a tab bar: Home | Timetable | Stats | Rank | Settings, and update app routing/state so switching tabs works smoothly without breaking existing navigation (including deep navigation to Subject Details).

Create/implement a Stats screen to support the new Stats tab with a clean, responsive layout and English text; the page must not be a dead-end and must render meaningful attendance summary data using existing local state/calculations (no new attendance logic).

Enhance the Rank screen UI to a modern, premium competitive leaderboard: display Top 3 users separately at the top with distinct gold/silver/bronze elevated cards (with smooth on-load animation); below Top 3, render all remaining users in a vertical list with dynamically generated rank numbers (4..N) shown as large, bold, gradient-styled numbers inside circular badges; no ranks may be hardcoded.

Add Rank screen interaction and UX enhancements: pull-to-refresh (or an explicit refresh control) to reload rankings; highlight the current logged-in user row with a glowing border and a “You” badge; add a subtle confetti animation when the current user is in the Top 3; and ensure a scrollable list that performs well with 100+ users (no jank, no overflow).

Ensure the frontend displays rankings in strict rank order with correct English empty/error states, and add offline-friendly behavior by caching the most recent successfully loaded weekly ranking locally and showing it when the backend cannot be reached (with clear English messaging that the data may be stale).

Replace the requested Firebase/Firestore global ranking backend with an Internet Computer (Motoko) canister-backed global ranking system that is readable by all users and writable only by the authenticated caller for their own user record, because Firebase/Firestore integration is not supported on this platform.

Upgrade the Rank screen data contract and UI rendering to display the required columns for every user in strict rank order: Rank Number (large, bold, circular gradient badge), User Name, College Name, Total Points, and Current Streak; keep the existing premium Top-3 section styling (gold/silver/bronze with crown/medal/award) and ensure the layout adapts correctly when there are fewer than 3 users.

Implement current-user highlighting and auto-scroll on Rank screen open: highlight the logged-in user’s row/card with a glow/border and a visible “You” badge, keep them at the correct rank position, and auto-scroll the list to bring the user into view when the Rank screen opens (when the user is not in the Top 3).

Add near-real-time leaderboard updates without WebSockets by implementing safe periodic refetching while the Rank screen is visible, plus the existing explicit refresh control as a secondary option; ensure cleanup to avoid memory leaks and preserve the offline-friendly cached fallback behavior with clear English messaging when showing stale data.

Implement scalable loading for 100+ users on the Rank screen by adding pagination or incremental loading in the frontend-to-backend ranking fetch flow, and ensure scrolling performance remains smooth with large lists (no overflow, no jank).

Create/align the ranking module structure under `frontend/src/rank` to follow a clean separation of concerns requested by the user by introducing (or updating) files that clearly map to: RankingModel, RankingRepository, RankingService, and RankingScreen (RankPage), while preserving existing behavior and routes.
Update the Login screen name input placeholder/example text to use "name_clg_sem" instead of the current example.

Update the Home dashboard quick-action buttons labeled “Mark Today’s Classes” and “View Rankings” to use the app’s purple primary styling (not black), ensuring the buttons appear purple in light mode, dark mode, and midnight theme.

Remove any device-specific or caller-only ranking behavior so the Rank screen always loads a truly global leaderboard from the Internet Computer canister (not from local cache/state), and ensure no code path filters rankings down to the current user only.

Fix pagination/incremental loading so that the Rank screen can scale to 100+ users without truncation, while still ensuring the UI can load and render the complete global ranking list (either via repeated page fetches until exhaustion or via an explicit 'load more' flow).
Ensure the Rank UI highlights the current logged-in user reliably (even if other users share the same display name) and auto-scrolls them into view when they are not in the Top 3.

Preserve near-real-time leaderboard updates without WebSockets by ensuring polling/refetching is safe (no memory leaks) and results remain consistent across devices; do not allow cached/stale data to override fresh global results when the backend is reachable.
Update all user-facing text in the ranking flow to be clear English, including explicit messaging when data is stale (cached fallback) or when the leaderboard cannot be loaded.

Add a Logout button in the Settings screen that, when confirmed, (1) deletes the current user from the backend ranking database and (2) erases all locally stored app data on the device, then returns the user to the Login screen.
Ensure the logout flow also logs the user out of Internet Identity so the next session starts unauthenticated.

Fix the post-logout “Unauthorized User” bug by making the logout flow immediately transition the UI to the Login screen, cancel/stop any in-flight backend calls, and prevent any subsequent backend calls from being initiated after logout completes.

Implement consistent, user-friendly handling for authorization-related backend errors so the app never shows raw “Unauthorized” text to users: map authorization failures to clean UX and recovery actions.

Harden the SettingsPage logout implementation to be resilient and ordered correctly: always clear device data (IndexedDB + ranking cache) and Internet Identity session without leaving the app in a partially logged-out state.

Upgrade the in-app notification settings UX to support separate notification preference categories (ranking alerts, reward alerts, streak reminders, etc.) within the existing supported web notification system, and persist these preferences via existing IndexedDB + backup/restore flows.

Improve reliability and clarity of the existing “Send Test Notification” action to ensure it consistently provides visible feedback for all states (supported/unsupported, enabled/disabled, permission granted/denied) without silent failure.

Document and enforce platform limitations in Settings → Notifications so users are not misled: explicitly state that this build supports browser notifications while the app is running and does not provide true background push delivery when the app is closed.

Update the shared frontend display-name validation to enforce the regex `^[A-Za-z0-9_ ]+$` (after trimming leading/trailing spaces), and when invalid return/show the exact English error message: "Only letters, numbers, spaces and underscore are allowed."

Ensure any user-facing frontend error displayed for invalid usernames uses the exact English string: "Only letters, numbers, spaces and underscore are allowed." (no commas, no extra punctuation, no alternate wording).

Add a new Dashboard quick-action button labeled exactly "Mark Past Attendance" placed below the existing "Mark Today's Classes" button, and wire it to open a dedicated past-attendance marking flow without rebuilding or removing existing flows.
Implement a calendar-based past-date selector for the "Mark Past Attendance" flow that allows selecting any previous date and prevents selecting future dates with clear English feedback.

For a selected past date, compute and display the scheduled subjects for that day using both (a) the weekly repeating timetable based on the date’s weekday and (b) any per-date overrides already supported by the app (for example, class exchanges tied to a specific date).
Allow the user to mark each scheduled subject for the selected past date as Present or Absent and save the attendance with the selected date, recording per-subject status plus a timestamp.

Enforce duplicate-marking prevention for past attendance: a user must not be able to mark the same date twice; if the date has already been marked, block saving and show the exact English message: "Attendance already marked for this date".

Integrate the past-attendance save into the frontend data model by creating corresponding ClassEvent entries (or an equivalent existing local event model) for the selected date so that existing calculations and UI (overall %, subject cards, subject details) reflect the saved past attendance without introducing new attendance-calculation logic.

Ensure streak and milestone points are recalculated correctly when past attendance is added: the existing continuous-day streak computation must reflect the newly added past date events, and milestone point awards must not be double-awarded for milestones that were already recorded as awarded.

Remove or disable any existing "auto-mark absent" or automatic missed-attendance penalty behavior so that if the user forgets to mark attendance, the system does nothing automatically and leaves the day unmodified.

Implement a once-per-day attendance reminder notification check: if the user has not marked today’s attendance by a fixed local time (default 7:00 PM), send a browser notification with Title exactly "Attendance Not Marked 📢" and Body exactly "You haven’t marked today’s attendance. Tap to update now.", respecting notification settings and sending at most once per calendar day.

When the user clicks the reminder notification (while the app is running), bring the app window into focus and open the attendance marking UI (the existing "Mark Today's Classes" sheet) so the user can update attendance immediately.

Persist the reminder-deduping state (for example, the last local date a reminder was sent) through the existing IndexedDB persistence and backup/restore flows in a backward-compatible way (merging missing fields with defaults).

Add clear English user-facing messaging in the past-attendance flow and reminder flow for all major error states (future date blocked, duplicate date, no subjects scheduled, notifications disabled/unsupported/permission denied), reusing existing toast/alert patterns.

Update the daily attendance reminder notification content to exactly match the required English strings when sent: Title exactly "Attendance Not Marked 📢" and Body exactly "You haven’t marked today’s attendance. Tap to update now.", and keep the reminder deduped to at most once per local calendar day using the existing settings.lastReminderDate mechanism.

Implement the reminder notification click behavior so that when the user clicks the reminder notification while the app is running, the app window is focused and the existing "Mark Today’s Classes" bottom sheet opens (without requiring a manual navigation by the user).

Harden the reminder scheduling/polling logic so it is safe and leak-free: only schedule checks when notifications are enabled AND the Streak Reminders category is enabled; ensure intervals are cleaned up on settings changes/unmount; and ensure the reminder check does not spam repeated attempts before 7:00 PM local time.

Add clear English, user-friendly, non-blocking feedback when the app is configured to send reminders but cannot send them due to browser limitations (unsupported Notifications API, permission denied/default, or notifications disabled), using the existing toast/alert patterns and avoiding repeated noisy messages.

Upgrade the existing calendar month header layout so the month label is centered and the navigation arrows are placed at the extreme left/right with proper horizontal padding, without changing any calendar functionality (date selection, disabled dates, navigation behavior). The header must use a flex layout equivalent to: left arrow | centered month text | right arrow, with `justify-between` behavior and minimum 16px horizontal padding, ensuring no overlap at any screen size.

Improve the calendar’s visual hierarchy and premium styling (layout-only): make the month label larger with semi-bold/bold weight and slight letter spacing; render navigation arrows as circular, touch-friendly icon buttons with a subtle border or soft glow and smooth hover/press animations. Do not change the click targets’ behavior or add new functionality.

Make the calendar container and day cells look premium with a dark modern theme and neon blue/violet accents, without changing functionality: (1) calendar container uses rounded corners (16–20px radius), subtle dark gradient background, 1px subtle border, and soft shadow/glow; (2) day cells have clear visual states—default dates in soft grey, today highlighted with a glow ring, selected date as a filled circle using the accent color, and disabled future dates shown with lower opacity; (3) add a smooth selection animation that does not cause layout shift.

Optimize the calendar UI for mobile responsiveness without changing functionality: ensure tap-friendly day cell sizing, adequate spacing between dates, no crowding/overflow, and responsive scaling across small screens. The calendar must remain performant (no jank) and must not introduce new timers or leaking intervals.

Fix the "Mark Past Attendance" flow so that selecting a past date immediately displays the scheduled subjects for that date (filtered by the selected date’s weekday + same-date exchange overrides), and the UI reliably transitions from date selection to the subject-marking step without closing/resetting unexpectedly.

Update the daily missed-attendance reminder notification body text to exactly: "You forgot to mark today's attendance. Tap to mark now." while keeping the reminder deduped to at most once per local calendar day and keeping the existing click behavior that focuses the app and opens the "Mark Today’s Classes" UI while the app is running.

Add clear English user-facing messaging in Settings → Notifications and/or relevant notification surfaces clarifying that this build supports browser notifications while the app is running and does not support Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) push notifications for background delivery on Web or Android within this platform build.

Fix the calendar header layout in the "Mark Past Attendance" modal so it has three clearly separated sections (Header navigation row, Weekday row, Date grid) with no overlap/collision, and the month title remains perfectly centered between left/right navigation arrows on all screen sizes.

Update the initial loading splash screen UI (frontend/src/components/system/InitialLoadSplash.tsx) to remove the purple/pink gradient background and instead use the app’s standard dark theme background color (same background styling used by the main app UI), while keeping the splash overlay behavior unchanged.

Adjust the splash screen layout to be a clean, minimal, fully centered logo presentation: center the logo both horizontally and vertically using a flex layout equivalent to `display:flex; justify-content:center; align-items:center; height:100vh`, with no extra padding/margins, and ensure the logo scales responsively without stretching or pixelation.

Replace the splash screen’s displayed logo asset with the newly finalized BunkPro logo by ensuring the splash uses the current branding-provided app icon path (BRANDING.getAppIcon) that points at the finalized asset under frontend/public/assets/generated, and remove the logo image from Settings → About (frontend/src/components/settings/AboutCard.tsx) so the About section shows only text details (app name/info/version/founder/copyright) without rendering any logo image.

Update the Dashboard UI (frontend/src/pages/HomeDashboardPage.tsx) to render a new card section placed below the existing Overall Attendance/Attendance Percentage card, titled exactly "Bunkable Classes", that displays the backend-calculated bunkable count for the current overall attendance (TotalClasses = overall attended + missed; AttendedClasses = overall attended).

Implement clean modern risk styling on the "Bunkable Classes" card using color indicators: Green = Safe, Orange = Risk, Red = Critical. Apply Red highlight when X = 0 or when attendance is below the required limit; apply Green highlight when attendance is very safe; otherwise apply Orange highlight.

Wire the dashboard bunkable-classes display to the backend for calculation and required percentage retrieval (do not rely only on frontend calculations). If the backend is unavailable or the call fails, fall back to a clear English non-blocking error state on the card while keeping the rest of the dashboard functional.

Eliminate any purple/pink background or gradient on the initial loading splash overlay by forcing a solid dark background color that matches the app’s dark theme (use a single solid color such as #0D0D0D), and ensure this background is applied regardless of current theme variables or Tailwind `bg-background` CSS variable values.

Prevent any pre-React-render “flash” of purple/pink by setting the initial document background to the same solid dark color used for the splash (e.g., via `frontend/index.html` and/or global base CSS for `html, body`), and add/update the browser theme color metadata so the browser UI does not show a purple theme tint during initial load.

Replace the splash screen logo with the user-uploaded finalized logo image `Bunkpro.logo_dark_mode.png` by adding it to `frontend/public/assets/generated/` and updating branding so `BRANDING.getAppIcon(...)` resolves to this uploaded asset (use the same asset for both dark and light to avoid mismatches).

Ensure the splash screen layout is a clean, minimal, fully centered logo presentation using a flex layout equivalent to `display:flex; justify-content:center; align-items:center; height:100vh`, with no extra padding/margins, and ensure the logo scales responsively.

Address caching/stale-asset root causes so the updated splash background and logo reliably appear after refresh by ensuring no old assets are referenced anywhere and by making the updated asset path the single source of truth for splash branding.

Update the app’s notification-related UI copy to clearly and consistently communicate that this build supports only browser Notifications API alerts while the app is running, and that Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM) push notifications (including background/app-closed delivery and Android APK push) are not supported in this platform build.
Completely remove the splash screen from the codebase by deleting `frontend/src/components/system/InitialLoadSplash.tsx` and removing all imports/usages/references to it across the app.

Remove any splash-related conditional render logic and any artificial initialization delays so the app renders the real first screen immediately (Login when logged out; Dashboard when logged in). Specifically remove the `isInitializing` state and the startup `setTimeout` delay currently gating the app UI in `frontend/src/App.tsx`.

Remove any initial loading/splash markup from the HTML entrypoint and public assets (e.g., any `#splash-screen` div, hardcoded loading spinner markup, or similar placeholders) so the only startup container is the React root.

Remove any splash-specific styling (CSS classes, inline styles, animations) so no leftover splash styles affect the app; keep a clean, solid dark initial background to avoid any pre-render background flash.

If the project includes any Service Worker / PWA precache behavior, update it so splash-related cached assets and any cached HTML that could reintroduce splash UI are not served; ensure the newest version loads immediately after deployment.

new_feature_requests.summary: Implement subject-wise attendance tracking with add/edit/delete subjects, reset attendance, and delete confirmation dialogs
Implement timetable creation (day-wise subjects) including extra classes and class exchanges
Implement class marking workflow: attended, missed/bunked, cancelled, with accurate subject-wise % calculations
